clue.text: Limo once cleared of external insects to give a rear view

indicators.note: with its outside letters cleared away, what is inside the words 'Limo once' (playing on in-sects, cut into) is kept

explanation.surface: A vintage limousine is fumigated of the bugs on its outside so the back looks presentable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared of external insects' says take the inner part of 'Limo once', where the letters run together in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooning is slang for baring one's buttocks at people, literally giving them a rear view.

indicators.note: the tense letter goes inside the rearranged letters
excited letters are stirred up, so the word messy is rearranged

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone describes a tense, agitated and untidy manner of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges MESSY to SYSEM, and 'in' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a method or way of doing something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Signature scrawled all over page, which is largely brilliant

indicators.note: the scrawled letters spread all over, surrounding the single page letter
scrawled writing is messy, so the letters of signature are jumbled

explanation.surface: An autograph is scribbled across a whole sheet, and the result is mostly dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrawled' rearranges SIGNATURE, and 'all over' wraps those letters around P.
explanation.definitionFit: A supergiant is a star of enormous size and luminosity, so it is brilliant on a large scale.

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits over, i.e. above, the next

parts.note: to slave is to toil, or sweat
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: Someone toils away over a South American tracksuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase, but South gives S and American belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage, sweats are a sweatsuit, the loose outfit British speakers call a tracksuit.

clue.text: Uneasy phone discussion not entirely conveyed

indicators.note: only part of the phrase uneasy phone discussion is used, the run of letters across its middle

explanation.surface: An awkward call is only partly passed on to others.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of 'Uneasy', all of 'phone' and the start of 'discussion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that is siphoned is drawn or carried off through a tube, so it is conveyed.

clue.text: Those who squeal about mark on horse

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: rats are informers, people who squeal to the authorities

explanation.surface: Informers talk about a mark found on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RATS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A white patch on a horse's forehead is called by this name, from its shape.

indicators.note: the shellfish word is placed round the river letter

parts.note: winkles are small edible sea snails
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone collects shellfish around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathers' reads as a verb of collecting, but it is the noun for folds or creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathers are small folds or puckers in fabric or skin, the same as creases.

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: an aggregate is a whole made up of parts

explanation.surface: A builder scrapes the surface layer off a pile of gravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' removes W from WHOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a scrape and this word mean an awkward predicament, a tight spot.

definitions.meaning: a curt command telling someone to go off now
describes somewhere that lies along your route, so you need not detour

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go, or told a place is handy to drop in at.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as a dismissal and as a description of something lying along one's route.

clue.text: Approximately to the right of top of tree trunk

indicators.note: in an across clue the second piece is written to the right of the first
the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

parts.note: or so means approximately, as in ten or so

explanation.surface: Something lies roughly right of the top of a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like part of the tree, but it means the human body without head and limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body is the part left without head, arms and legs.

parts.note: a nit is a louse egg, a parasite
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A parasite sits on a component of plant food.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre (potassium nitrate) has long been used as a nitrogen-rich ingredient in fertilisers.

clue.text: Observant quality present in fluid dance

indicators.note: the word for present is set inside the rearranged letters
fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters of dance are rearranged

parts.note: to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A dancer's watchfulness shows during a flowing routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observant' looks like watchful, but here it means keeping to rules; 'fluid' makes ADNCE, which 'in' wraps round the word for present.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant here means keeping to rules or customs, and close observance of them is called this.

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
to get on is to grow older, or age

explanation.surface: A mother takes over for the planet Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like the planet or the chocolate bar, but it is the verb meaning spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or harm it, the same as to damage.

indicators.note: moving letters are shifted around, so the remainder is rearranged
no means the alternative word is removed from forward

parts.note: or is the word introducing an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful advances, with no other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes OR from FORWARD, leaving FWARD, and 'moving' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is one of the seven small companions of Snow White, an example of the type.

clue.text: Stars from here backing Elton at city in America?

indicators.note: backing means the word is reversed

parts.note: Ben Elton is a British comedian and writer

indicators.note: the city letters go inside the country letters

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A star singer called Elton heads back to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elton' suggests the singer Elton John, but it is comedian Ben Elton's surname, so BEN, which 'backing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: These clouds of gas and dust are where new stars are born.

indicators.note: the letters of kebab stall are made ready in a new order, as food is prepared

explanation.surface: A food stall has a kebab ready for the match crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a team sport played with a ball and hoops, an example of a game.

clue.text: Sort of power that lifts Los Alamos Red Tops

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word turns it upwards, reading it backwards
the tops of the words in a down clue are their first letters

explanation.surface: A kind of energy powers the Los Alamos laboratory and the red-top tabloids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' turns LOS upwards, and 'Tops' takes A and R from Alamos and Red. 'Red Tops' looks like Britain's red-mastheaded tabloid papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy from the sun is a type of power used in panels and cells.

clue.text: Car — middle of fan belt lacks power

indicators.note: the middle of a three-letter word is its central letter
lacks means the power letter is removed

parts.note: a strap is a belt
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A car's broken fan belt has left it without power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes P from STRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vauxhall (Opel) Astra is a popular family car model.

clue.text: Brown needs one inch A-Z up country

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read backwards

parts.note: a means one
A-Z gives the two letters A and Z

explanation.surface: A man called Brown needs a street atlas to find his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AINAZ to ZANIA. The A-Z is a well-known British street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an East African nation, an example of a country.

parts.note: in snooker this ball is potted again and again, and being worth a single point it is the lightest in value

explanation.surface: Something light enough is often slipped into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker, a cue game like pool, has fifteen balls of this colour, each worth one point.
explanation.definitionFit: The most frequently potted snooker ball is the one-point ball of this colour.

parts.note: rolling in it means rich
a ness is a cape or headland, the 's linking it

explanation.surface: A headland's grandeur is a rolling one.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence or splendour is another word for magnificence.

clue.text: Elvis is alive, full of fibre!

indicators.note: the phrase Elvis is alive holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A conspiracy believer insists Elvis lives, with a joke about fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of fibre' looks like a diet phrase, but 'full of' says the letters are held within 'Elvis is alive'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Nut cracking, in fact, absorbs one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or absorb, the letter for one
cracking breaks up the letters of in fact into a new order

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A nut is cracked and in fact soaks something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' rearranges IN FACT, and 'absorbs' takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is an enthusiast or zealot, someone obsessive about a pursuit.

definitions.meaning: a spy planted long in advance and left inactive until needed
a railway tie, which lies beneath the rails of the line

explanation.surface: A spy's item is accounted for below the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below-the-line' sounds like accounting jargon, but means beneath a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dormant spy and a beam supporting railway track.

definitions.note: Sherlock's here means Sherlock is, so the definition is the detective himself

indicators.note: the rearranged letters break into the silence letters

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: playing the lute shakes up its letters

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes strums an instrument and shatters the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes played the violin, not the lute, so 'playing' is a scramble signal; 'breaks' puts the result between the two letters of the hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is fiction's most famous detective, the archetype of an investigator.

clue.text: Composed some material in C? The other way round

indicators.note: the clue says material in C, signalling one piece goes inside another
this reverses the nesting just described, so C goes inside the material

parts.note: plaid is a tartan cloth

explanation.surface: A musician composed a piece in the key of C, then reversed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in C' then 'The other way round' means C goes in PLAID, not the reverse. 'Composed' looks musical, but it means calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone composed is calm and unruffled, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Test space craft with no tail

indicators.note: the tail is the last letter, which is removed

parts.note: Challenger was a NASA space shuttle

explanation.surface: A spacecraft is tested after losing its tail section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no tail' removes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenge is a demanding task that tests ability, a synonym.

clue.text: Try to single someone out, as prolific anglers do

definitions.meaning: drawing straws or similar to pick one person by chance
keen anglers throw their lines into the water many times

explanation.surface: A selection process is compared to fishermen at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to choose by chance, and cryptically to throw a line many times.

indicators.note: the champion word is placed outside the left letter

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it

explanation.surface: A sports champion plays at outside left, with a grim sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside left' looks like a football position, but 'outside' puts BACK round L.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of comedy finds humour in grim subjects such as death.

indicators.note: over means turned over, reversing the word

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look over' reads as inspect, but 'over' reverses PEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: The central stronghold of a castle is a tower of this name.

definitions.meaning: a loose straight dress hanging from the shoulders
to move something from one place to another

explanation.surface: A garment is moved on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a simple loose dress and also means to move or transfer.

clue.text: Attendant puts a report in place

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place
to tell is to report

explanation.surface: A helper slots a report into its proper place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attendant' looks like a person, but here it means a follower or hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a follower or dependant that attends a larger figure.
